narrative.overview:
A logbook is written while the work is happening, by someone who expects to be held to it. It is ruled, dated, and numbered. Nothing in it is staged for a reader, which is exactly why a reader trusts it. This system takes that posture: the page is a record, not a pitch, and it assumes the visitor is capable of reading one.

Everything follows from that. Structure comes from ruled lines rather than boxes, because a ledger is ruled. Keys, versions, dates and counts are set in monospace because they are data being logged, not decoration borrowed to look technical. Colour is rationed to state — what is available, what is current, what is live — since a log that highlights everything has recorded nothing.

The design is deliberately unfashionable. It rejects the current portfolio house style outright: no rounded status pills, no chip rows, no pulsing dots, no coloured bar down the side of a card, no highlighter behind a word.
keyCharacteristics: Ruled, not boxed — hairlines separate, containers don't enclose
Zero shadows, zero radius on panels; 3px only on small controls
Monospace for data, sans for prose, Ethiopic first-class in both
One accent, spent only on state
Two themes measured independently, never inverted from each other

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Instrument Green marks state and nothing else: available, current, live. Never general emphasis. When a thing needs weight, use weight.

rules.name: The Two-Ground Rule
rules.body: A colour is verified against the surface it actually lands on, not against the page. An accent validated on the ground says nothing about the same accent on a 12% tint of itself — that exact mistake produced seven AA failures.

rules.name: The Borrowed-Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: The four tag hues are quoted from release notes, not this system's palette. They stay inside change tags; promoting one to a section colour breaks the quotation.

rules.name: The Sixteen-Pixel Floor
rules.body: Body text is never below 16px. 14px is permitted only for genuinely secondary metadata.

rules.name: The Monospace-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks information that is logged, measured or versioned. Never applied to prose to look technical — that is costume.

rules.name: The Dark-Compensation Rule
rules.body: Light text on dark reads tighter and thinner. Reading text on dark gains leading (1.6 to 1.7) and tracking (0.006em). Never ship dark as a pure inversion.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow anywhere, in any state, including hover and focus. Separate with a rule or a surface step.

rules.name: The One-Declaration Rule
rules.body: An element declares elevation once. A 1px border under a soft shadow is the ghost card; pick the border.

rules.name: The No-Card Rule
rules.body: A rounded, shadowed rectangle is not how this system groups things. Group with rules and space.

rules.name: The Side-Bar Ban
rules.body: A coloured border-left or border-top above 1px on a card, panel or callout is forbidden outright. No brief earns it back.

dos: Do spend Instrument Green on state only — available, current, live.
Do verify every colour against the surface it actually sits on, and measure both themes independently.
Do keep body text at 16px or above, and prose within a 66ch measure.
Do use monospace for logged data — versions, dates, keys, counts — and sans for anything read in sentences.
Do separate with hairlines and space; let the tonal step from ground to surface carry what little depth exists.
Do prefix every modifier class with is-. Tailwind's utilities are global via style.css, so a bare fixed or hidden silently pulls an element out of its layout.
Do use padding-block on any section that also carries .cl-shell; the padding shorthand overrides the shell's gutter and the section goes edge-to-edge on mobile.
Do give prefers-reduced-motion a real alternative: stop ambient loops outright, keep transitions at 1ms so state still reports.
donts: Don't use rounded status pills, chip rows or pulsing dots as page furniture.
Don't put a coloured border-left or border-top above 1px on any card, panel or callout. Banned outright.
Don't emphasise a word with a highlighter or gradient behind it.
Don't add a box-shadow anywhere, in any state.
Don't write metaphor-forward copy. Claims are direct and checkable.
Don't introduce a font size or spacing value outside the two scales.
Don't animate anything ambient beyond the single live-status pulse, and never animate a layout property.
